title: From Model Assurance to Causal Answerability: A Multi-Timescale Information Architecture for Governed Agentic AI
content: Agentic artificial intelligence turns model outputs into state-changing commitments, making model-level evaluation necessary but insufficient for governance. This article develops a causal answerability architecture that connects three timescales: pre-deployment capability assurance, in-actu admissibility control, and post-action consequence reconciliation. An integrative design-science synthesis draws on cybernetics, reference-monitor security, runtime assurance, provenance standards, dynamic safety cases, algorithmic accountability, and governance-native computing. The central result is a commitment graph that represents purpose, principals, authority, policies, evidence, expected effects, provenance, observed consequences, obligations, and remedies as persistent governance information. Seven design invariants are derived: complete mediation, actor-independent validation, tamper-evident provenance, independent consequence observation, obligation persistence, safe fallback and repair, and contestable institutional authority. The architecture treats models, humans, services, and tools as replaceable actors rather than sovereign owners of policy or history. It also reframes coherence debt as a domain-calibrated vector of authority, evidence, provenance, consequence, continuity, and repair deficits. Testable hypotheses, implementation metrics, and adversarial stress tests are specified. The article does not claim that any single implementation has established general superiority; rather, it offers a falsifiable information architecture for coupling frontier assurance to runtime control and delayed institutional learning.
